issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks from CI workaround into core/setup.py runtime install_requires.
issues.detail: The mmcv pkg_resources problem is a build-time CI issue, but pinning setuptools<82 in core/setup.py forces every downstream user of autogluon to accept the cap forever. The constraint belongs only in the CI scripts where the FIXME already lives. Wrong scope: a CI hack stapled onto the package's runtime dependencies.

issues.description: Silent mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 bump bundled into a setuptools fix with no justification.
issues.detail: The PR is titled as an mmengine/setuptools fix but quietly bumps mmdet a minor version. Separate decision, separate risk surface. If 3.3.0 is required for compatibility with mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0, state it in the diff; otherwise split into its own change so it can be bisected later.

issues.description: --no-build-isolation silently couples mmcv build to ambient setuptools/torch without stated precondition.
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation means mmcv reads whatever setuptools, torch, and ninja are in the active env. It works because setuptools<82 is pinned the line before and torch is preinstalled by the caller, but the ordering invariant is invisible. Add an inline comment stating the precondition so a reorder doesn't silently break the build.

issues.description: Three independent setuptools<82 pins with no single source of truth.
issues.detail: env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py each independently assert setuptools<82 referencing the same upstream mmcv issue. When mmcv#3325 is fixed, someone must remember all three sites; the FIXME comment isn't even present in all of them. A shared constant or script would let one edit revert the workaround cleanly.

issues.description: FIXME comments lack revert criteria or owner for lifting the setuptools cap.
issues.detail: The FIXMEs reference mmcv#3325 but state no condition that flips the cap off (e.g., "once mmcv ships a wheel that doesn't import pkg_resources at build time") and no owner. Six months from now a grep for FIXME forces reverse-engineering the trigger. Add the explicit revert condition.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The CI fix itself is reasonable — pin setuptools<82 to dodge the pkg_resources removal that breaks mmcv's build, install mmengine from PyPI instead of a git SHA — but the patch does more than one thing. The setuptools cap leaks into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires, imposing a CI workaround on every downstream user of autogluon. A silent mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 minor bump rides along with no rationale and should be split. Three independent copies of the pin with no shared source of truth and FIXMEs without revert criteria guarantee this debt rots.
